title: Height of a bamboo shoot over six weeks
bodyMd: A gardener measured the height of a single bamboo shoot once a week for six weeks. The scatterplot shows the six measurements, and a line of best fit for the data has the equation $h = 7.2w + 4.8$, where $h$ is the height in centimetres and $w$ is the number of weeks since the first measurement.

data.caption: Weekly height of one bamboo shoot, with line of best fit h = 7.2w + 4.8.

accessibilityText: A scatterplot of bamboo shoot height against week, with six plotted points and a rising straight line of best fit. The horizontal axis is the week number from 1 to 6 and the vertical axis is height in centimetres from 0 to 50. The six points are: week 1, 12 centimetres; week 2, 19 centimetres; week 3, 27 centimetres; week 4, 33 centimetres; week 5, 41 centimetres; week 6, 48 centimetres. The line of best fit has equation h equals 7.2 times w plus 4.8.

provenance.notes: Original data written for this item bank. The line of best fit was computed by least squares from these six invented points, so the stated equation genuinely matches the data.
